issue.body:
### Describe the bug

If a kernel writes a global buffer and then reads the same buffer back, `tritongpu-coalesce` can hand the store and the load different layouts. When that happens one thread reads back what another thread wrote, and there's no barrier in between, so it's a data race and the output comes out wrong (and different from run to run).

In the original code the store and the load share the same pointer and layout, so each thread just reads its own data. Coalesce is what splits them: it clamps the store to 128 bits per thread but leaves a load in the same group wider, and `warpsPerCTA` follows from that. `Membar` doesn't help, since it only  tracks shared memory and never sees a global buffer round-trip.

Repro with `triton-opt repro.mlir -tritongpu-coalesce`:

  ```mlir
  #blocked = #ttg.blocked<{sizePerThread = [1, 1], threadsPerWarp = [1, 32], warpsPerCTA = [1, 4], order = [1, 0]}>
  module attributes {"ttg.num-ctas" = 1 : i32, "ttg.num-warps" = 4 : i32, "ttg.threads-per-warp" = 32 : i32} {
    tt.func public @rb(%arg0: !tt.ptr<f32> {tt.divisibility = 16 : i32}, %arg1: !tt.ptr<f16> {tt.divisibility = 16 : i32}) {
      %cst = arith.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<8x256xf32, #blocked>
      %r = tt.make_range {end = 256 : i32, start = 0 : i32} : tensor<256xi32, #ttg.slice<{dim = 0, parent = #blocked}>>
      %re = tt.expand_dims %r {axis = 0 : i32} : tensor<256xi32, #ttg.slice<{dim = 0, parent = #blocked}>> -> tensor<1x256xi32, #blocked>
      %off = tt.broadcast %re : tensor<1x256xi32, #blocked> -> tensor<8x256xi32, #blocked>
      // a wide f16 load in the same block makes the group read layout [1, 8]
      %sp16 = tt.splat %arg1 : !tt.ptr<f16> -> tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f16>, #blocked>
      %p16 = tt.addptr %sp16, %off : tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f16>, #blocked>, tensor<8x256xi32, #blocked>
      %w = tt.load %p16 : tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f16>, #blocked>
      // write arg0, then read it back with the same pointer
      %sp = tt.splat %arg0 : !tt.ptr<f32> -> tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f32>, #blocked>
      %p = tt.addptr %sp, %off : tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f32>, #blocked>, tensor<8x256xi32, #blocked>
      tt.store %p, %cst : tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f32>, #blocked>
      %v = tt.load %p : tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f32>, #blocked>
      tt.return
    }
  }
  ```
The store comes out `sizePerThread = [1, 4], warpsPerCTA = [2, 2]` and the read-back `sizePerThread = [1, 8], warpsPerCTA = [4, 1]` - same memory, but the two layouts give the same element to different threads, with nothing synchronizing them. I'd expect the store and its read-back to keep one layout, or to have a barrier between them.

### Environment details

Triton: latest
issue.title: Coalesce gives a store and its read-back different layouts (data race)

issue.body:
Coalesce picks a layout per op, so a store and a later load of the same buffer can get different layouts, and a thread reads back what another wrote (no barrier between them).

Fix: when a store and a load address the same `(arg, offset)`, give the store the load's layout so the round-trip stays within a thread.

Fixes #10924.

issue.body:
## Motivation

`workflow.prepare_issue_set` assembles exact issue facts, coverage, related
work, precedents, and conservative linkage candidates. That is the right
evidence boundary, but the caller still has to translate those records into a
pre-implementation action for every issue.

In a recent Triton workflow, implementation worktrees were created before that
translation happened. Subsequent thread and pull-request inspection showed
three materially different dispositions:

| Target | Upstream evidence | Appropriate action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#11047](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/issues/11047) | Closing PR [#11056](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11056) was already merged | Do not start another implementation |
| [#10924](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/issues/10924) | Closing PR [#10925](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/10925) was closed unmerged after maintainer discussion | Re-establish desired semantics before coding |
| [#10950](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/issues/10950) | Closing PR [#11041](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11041) was closed unmerged and the accepted contract took a different direction | Re-establish desired semantics before coding |

The evidence was discoverable, but it arrived after workspace dispatch. This is
not a request for GitContribute to infer technical correctness or to turn
maintainer prose into an automatic rejection. It is a request for a
conservative, source-backed contribution disposition at the exact-issue-set
boundary, where an agent is deciding whether to investigate, coordinate, or
create a workspace.

## Proposed Solution

Extend exact issue-set preparation, or add a closely scoped offline operation,
that derives a conservative disposition and next action from stored,
coverage-qualified facts.

A possible result model is:

```text
issue
  state: open | closed
  contribution_disposition:
    status: ready_to_investigate
          | active_competing_work
          | already_resolved_upstream
          | needs_maintainer_alignment
          | blocked_by_repository_policy
          | unknown
    confidence: high | medium | low
    evidence_refs: [...]
    unknowns: [...]
    next_action: ...
```

The derivation should be deliberately conservative:

- a merge-confirmed closing PR can establish `already_resolved_upstream`;
- a complete open-PR population containing an active closing implementation
  can establish `active_competing_work`;
- a closed-unmerged linked PR plus hydrated maintainer discussion can establish
  `needs_maintainer_alignment`, but not automatically `blocked`;
- a documented duplicate, not-planned, archived, or contribution-policy
  condition may establish an explicit blocked state;
- an open issue with no known related work is at most
  `ready_to_investigate`, not `ready_to_code`; and
- incomplete headers, missing merge outcome, absent comments, or stale
  repository guidance must produce `unknown` or a weaker disposition with an
  exact recovery action.

Maintainer-direction evidence should retain the author association, exact
source URL, observation revision, and a bounded extract. Free-form prose should
not be converted into a stronger status than deterministic evidence supports.

The operation should remain offline. Suggested sync or hydration calls should
remain explicit, just as they are for `workflow.prepare_issue_set`.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Require every client to interpret `prepare_issue_set` independently.**
  This preserves the current tool surface but repeats a high-consequence
  composition and makes late workspace creation mistakes more likely.
- **Use Radar eligibility for exact issues.** Radar ranks a bounded open-issue
  population; exact issue-set preparation also needs closed targets,
  merge-confirmed outcomes, and per-target recovery guidance.
- **Treat any closed linked PR as a blocker.** Closed-unmerged work may be
  abandoned, superseded, or rejected for an approach-specific reason. It
  requires a coordination state, not an invented repository decision.
- **Make workspace creation perform hidden GitHub reads.** That violates the
  explicit side-effect boundary and makes workspace behavior depend on network
  availability.

## Impact

This affects the workflow/research composition over existing corpus evidence.
It should not mutate GitHub, create opportunities or workspaces, execute
repository code, or claim that a proposed implementation satisfies an issue.

Acceptance criteria:

- exact issue-set preparation can return a bounded disposition and next action
  per issue;
- every non-unknown disposition has source references and qualifying coverage;
- incomplete or stale evidence never becomes a ready or resolved conclusion;
- merged closing work, open competing work, closed-unmerged work, explicit
  repository rejection, and no-related-work cases remain distinct;
- concise output stays bounded while detailed output exposes the supporting
  relation evidence; and
- tests cover the three Triton-shaped cases above plus missing comments,
  unknown merge outcome, stale coverage, and contradictory evidence.

issue.body:
## The bug

`tritongpu-coalesce` groups memory accesses by shape and order and then gives the
whole group the widest per-thread element count any member reached.  When one
access reads back a pointer another access in the group writes, the two must
agree on which thread owns which element: there is no barrier between them, so a
disagreement is a data race and the result is wrong and run-dependent (#10924).

For the kernel in the issue - an f32 store whose pointer is read back, with an
f16 load sharing the shape and order in the same block - the coalescer produces

```
tt.store %10, %11 : tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f32>, #blocked2>   ; sizePerThread [1,4]
%13 = tt.load %12  : tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f32>, #blocked1>   ; sizePerThread [1,8]
```

The 128-bit-per-thread limit on vectorized stores is what splits them: the f16
load legitimately reaches 8 elements per thread, the f32 store is clamped to 4,
and the f32 read-back load kept the group's 8.

## The fix

Detect the aliasing load explicitly - a load whose memory access pointer is one a
store in the same group writes - and clamp it to that store's own width instead
of to the group maximum.  Loads that merely share the shape and order keep the
width they are entitled to, since the group is not keyed on memory.

With the fix both ops come out `#blocked2`:

```
tt.store %10, %11 : tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f32>, #blocked2>
%13 = tt.load %12  : tensor<8x256x!tt.ptr<f32>, #blocked2>
```

## Testing

Adds a `tritongpu-coalesce` case to `test/TritonGPU/coalesce.mlir` asserting the
store and its read-back share one layout.  The lit suite passes with the new case
(the only failure in the run is a pre-existing test that requires
`TRITON_BUILD_UT=ON`).

## Performance

No regression: an interleaved A/B on a matched binary pair (only
`CoalesceUtils.cpp` differing) gives identical checksums for matmul, softmax and
stream kernels and timings within noise.

Fixes #10924

issue.title: [GPU] Preserve safe layouts for dependent global store/read-back

issue.body:
Global-memory accesses through the same pointer need not keep the same element-to-thread layout. This documents explicit block synchronization with `tl.debug_barrier()` and adds a read-back test that exchanges the two halves of each block.

This replaces the incorrect coalescer assumption in #11870. It changes documentation and tests only; it does not clamp load/store layouts or claim to fix a compiler bug. Related to #10924.

## Test results

| Check | Existing compiler behavior | Added coverage |
|---|---|---|
| Dependent read-back with an explicit barrier | Supported; no compiler change needed | 4/4 passed: block sizes 256/1024 × 4/8 warps |
| Values after exchanging the two block halves | Dense expected values | Exact match, `rtol=0`, `atol=0` |
| NVIDIA barrier emission | `tl.debug_barrier()` lowering | `bar.sync` present in generated PTX |
| Unsynchronized read-back | Not a correctness guarantee | Not used as a passing oracle |

```bash
python -m pytest -s --tb=short python/test/unit/language/test_core.py::test_debug_barrier_global_readback
```

Source baseline: `01c5d2ac6af3a314839ac6cc5787f71f90ffdb36` (main). SSH validation used Python 3.13.14, Torch 2.10.0+cu128 and the Triton 3.8.0 native wheel with the changed main Python files. The native compiler was not rebuilt. GPU tests ran on NVIDIA L20. The main versions of `_internal_testing.py`, `_compile_warmup_state.py` and `tools/mxfp.py` were used with the wheel for test/API compatibility.

Ruff 0.9.1, YAPF 0.43.0 and `git diff --check` passed. No performance change is claimed.
